what_this_is: Grok asked to review the uncommitted change while Codex was over its usage limit. Recorded because every paid call is recorded when it is made, whatever it returned.
what_this_is_not: A review. The one call that produced an answer made ZERO tool calls and never opened the diff; what it returned names a flag that does not exist (`check_accounted.py --frozen`) and places `wait_for_fresh_window` in a file it is not in. It is not evidence about the code and nothing in the change was altered on the strength of it.
why_a_floor: Only `--output-format streaming-json` emits the row that carries a cost. Eight invocations used the default format and priced nothing, so this figure is what three of eleven calls cost and not what the eleven cost.
billing_arrangement: SuperGrok Lite, EUR 20 a month, flat. One more call moves no bill; this figure is list price charged to nobody.

priced_calls.outcome: the tool call was CANCELLED by plan mode
completed; this is how the cancellation above was identified

what_was_learnt: `grok -p` does run an agent loop with tools; the owner corrected me on this.

The default permission behaviour is `ask`, and in a non-interactive session nobody answers, so the run ends having touched nothing and prints only its opening sentence. `--always-approve` is required.
`--permission-mode plan` does not restrict tools to reading — it CANCELS them. The stream says `User cancelled the execution` and `stopReason: cancelled`.

Without `--output-format streaming-json` none of this is visible: an early test appeared to succeed because the model answered `main` from inference, and only the stream showed there had been no tool call at all.
